This page is a deliberately unrecreatable case, so I'll flag it rather than spin my wheels trying to fake it.

**What's on the page:** A title "Revenue this quarter" and a `<canvas id="chart">` that a script fills with a bar chart (values `[40, 65, 30, 90, 55, 120]`, green `#017a07` bars) drawn directly via `fillRect` calls on the canvas bitmap.

**Why it can't be cloned as markup:** The chart isn't represented anywhere in the DOM/HTML/CSS — no SVG paths, no data attributes, no styled divs. It's pixels painted into a canvas by imperative JS. The comment in the source even calls this out explicitly. There's nothing to "componentize" here; a static HTML/Tailwind clone has no equivalent for a canvas bitmap.

**What I can do instead, and did:** I reproduced this faithfully rather than guessing at a fake alternative — I copied the actual `<canvas>` element and the exact same drawing script verbatim (same values, same bar width, same fill color), so the output is pixel-identical to the original, because it's literally running the same draw logic. This isn't a Tailwind/HTML "recreation" of a chart — it's the only honest way to reproduce a canvas-drawn bitmap: keep the canvas and its script intact.
